Rashi on Pesachim 6b:10:1.hebrew: אי הכי - קשיא לך — אפילו בתרי ענייני תיקשי לך, דהא דיינינן כלל ופרט כשנאמר אחד מהן בפרשה זו ואחד מהן בפרשה אחרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:10:1.english: If so - [Since] it is difficult for you, it should also be difficult for you even with regard to two matters, for we derive [by the rule of] a generalization and a detail when one of them is stated in this passage and one of them in another passage.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:10:2.english: This works out well - That it is not difficult for you.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:10:3.hebrew: למאן דאמר כלל ופרט המרוחקין אין דנין כו' - ופלוגתא היא במנחות בפרק כל המנחות באות מצה (מנחות דף נה:), ובבבא קמא בהחובל (בבא קמא דף פה.):
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:10:3.english: According to the one who said: A generalization and a detail that are removed [from one another], one does not derive, etc. - And it is a dispute in Menachot in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaMenachot Ba'ot Matzah (Menachot 55b), and in Bava Kamma in [the chapter entitled] HaChovel (Bava Kamma 85a).

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:12:1.hebrew: הבודק צריך שיבטל - בלבו, סמוך לבדיקה מיד, ואומר: "כל חמירא דאיכא בביתא הדין ליבטיל":
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:12:1.english: One who searches must nullify [it] - In his heart, immediately following the search, and he says: "All leaven that is in this house shall be nullified."

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:12:2.english: What is the reason - Behold, he destroys all that is found.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:13:1.hebrew: וכי תימא כיון דמנטר להו אגב ביתיה - עם שאר ממונו הוא משמרן, שכשהוא נועל ביתו לשומרו נמצא משמר כל מה שבתוכו, הלכך חשיבי. ושימור דלאו אדעתא דידיה הוא — מי מחשבי ליה?:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:13:1.english: And lest you say: Since they are protected on account of his house - Together with the rest of his property he protects them, for when he locks his house to protect it, he ends up protecting everything inside it; therefore, they are significant. And [yet,] does protection that is not intended for it render it significant?

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:13:2.hebrew: והתניא סופי תאנים - סוף לקיטת תאנים, נמצאים בתאנה תאנים שאינן מתבשלות כל צרכן עולמית:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:13:2.english: And wasn't it taught: The end of the figs - [At the] end of the fig harvest, there are figs found on the fig tree that never fully ripen.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:13:3.hebrew: ומשמר שדהו מפני ענבים - ובעל הבית זה משמר שדה זו שלא יכנסו בני אדם לתוכה, ואין דעתו מפני התאנים, אלא מפני שיש בה ענבים שעדיין לא הגיע עת הבציר. או סופי ענבים שלא יתבשלו עולמית, ובעל הבית משמר שדהו זו שהן בתוכה, ולא בשבילן, אלא מפני מדלעות ומקשאות שבה:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:13:3.english: And guards his field on account of the grapes - And this homeowner guards this field so that people will not enter it, and his intent is not [to guard it] on account of the figs, but rather because there are grapes in it whose time of grape harvest has not yet arrived. Or, [the second clause refers to] late grapes that will never ripen, and the homeowner guards this field of his in which they are [located], and [he does so] not for their sake, but rather on account of the gourds and cucumbers that are in it.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:13:4.english: Cucumbers and gourds - [The baraita] recites [further]: “All the trees.”

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:14:1.english: And they are obligated in tithe - If the owner gathered them or gave them to another.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:14:2.english: And [they are] exempt from the tithe - For ownerless property is exempt from the tithe.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:15:1.hebrew: ודעתו עליה - חשובה היא בעיניו, וחס עליה לשורפה, ומשהה אפילו רגע אחד, ונמצא עובר עליה בבל יראה ובבל ימצא. אבל משבטלה — אינו עובר, דלא כתב אלא תשביתו:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:15:1.english: And his thoughts are upon it - It is valuable in his eyes, and he spares it from being burned, and delays [destroying it] even a single moment, and consequently violates [the prohibitions of] “it shall not be seen” and “it shall not be found” on its account. But once he has nullified it, he does not violate [them], for [the Torah] wrote only: “You shall cause to cease.”

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:16:1.english: For it is not in his possession - It does not belong to him.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:16:2.hebrew: דאמר ר' אלעזר ב' דברים אינן שלו ועשאן הכתוב כאילו הן ברשותו - להתחייב עליהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:16:2.english: As Rabbi Elazar said: Two things are not his, and Scripture treated them as though they were in his possession - To be held liable for them:

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:16:3.hebrew: בור ברשות הרבים - הפותחו חייב בניזקין, ואין הבור שלו אלא של הפקר, שהרי ברשות הרבים הוא, ואף על פי שכרהו — אין רשות הרבים קנויה לו:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:16:3.english: A pit in the public domain - The one who opens it is liable for damages, and the pit is not his, but rather [is] ownerless, for it is in the public domain; and even though he dug it, the public domain is not acquired by him.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:17:1.hebrew: וניבטליה בארבע - כלומר, למה הוצרכתו לבטל בלילה? ליתקנו רבנן לכל אדם שיבטל קודם איסורו:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:17:1.english: And let him nullify it at the fourth [hour] - That is to say: Why did you require him to nullify [it] at night? Let the Rabbis institute for every person that he nullify [it] before its prohibition:

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:17:2.hebrew: פשע - ישכח ויבא לידי פשיעה, שעל ידי מה יזכר? אבל עכשיו, שעסוק בבדיקתו, יזכר:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:17:2.english: He will be negligent - He will forget and come to negligence, for by what means would he remember? But now, when he is engaged in searching for it, he will remember.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:1:1.hebrew: שהרי משה רבינו עומד בפסח ראשון - ודורש להן בהלכות פסח השני, דהיינו שלשים יום, שהוא בארבעה עשר באייר:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:1:1.english: For Moses our teacher was standing at the first Pesaḥ - And expounding to them the laws of the second Pesaḥ, which is thirty days [in advance], as it is on the fourteenth of Iyyar.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:6:1.english: Just as there [it was on] the New Moon - For it is written concerning it: “On the first of the second month.”

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:7:1.hebrew: וניכתוב ברישא כו' - לא אשמעתין פריך, אלא אסדר פרשיות קפריך: מכדי פרשת פסח נאמרה תחלה, שהרי בחדש הראשון נאמר, כדכתיב "בחדש הראשון לאמר", ופרשת פקודים נאמרה באייר — ומאי טעמא אקדמה להאי בראש הספר, ופרשת זו בפרשת בהעלותך:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:7:1.english: And let [the Torah] write first, etc. - [The Gemara] is not objecting to our teaching, but rather it is objecting to the order of the portions: After all, the portion of the Paschal offering was spoken first, for it was spoken in the first month, as it is written: “in the first month... saying,” and the portion of the census was spoken in Iyyar. And what is the reason that [the Torah] placed this one earlier, at the beginning of the book, and [placed] this portion in Parashat Beha'alotekha?

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:7:2.hebrew: אין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה - לא הקפידה תורה על סדר מוקדם ומאוחר, ופרשיות דנאמרו תחלה הקדימו המאוחרות לה:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:7:2.english: There is no earlier and later in the Torah - The Torah was not particular about the order of earlier and later, and [as for] sections that were stated first, the later ones preceded them.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:8:1.english: In two matters - In two [separate] sections.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:8:2.english: Within one matter - In verses arranged in a single passage.

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:8:3.hebrew: דאי לא תימא הכי - דבסדר כתיבתן נאמרו: הא דקיימא לן ״כל כלל ופרט אין בכלל אלא מה שהוא בפרט״ — לפי שבא הפרט ופרט שזהו הכלל — היכי סמכינן עלה? דילמא פרט וכלל הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:8:3.english: For if you do not say so - That they were stated in the order of their writing: [As for] that which is established for us, that [with] every generalization and detail, there is in the generalization only that which is in the detail — because the detail came and specified that this is the generalization — how could we rely on it? Perhaps it is a detail and a generalization!

Rashi on Pesachim 6b:9:1.hebrew: נעשה כלל מוסף על הפרט - שלא תאמר: אין כאן אלא פרט, או כיוצא בו נביא בדינו בבנין אב — לכן הוסיף הכתוב כלל אחריו, להביא כל דבר, ואפילו אינו דומה לפרט:
Rashi on Pesachim 6b:9:1.english: The generalization becomes an addition to the detail - So that you should not say: There is only the detail here, or [only that which is] similar to it do we bring under its law through a binyan av [paradigm] — therefore, Scripture added a generalization after it to include everything, even [that which] is not similar to the detail.

Tosafot on Pesachim 6b:11:1.hebrew: אבל בתרי ענייני אין דנין - והא דפריך בסוף הפרה (ב"ק ד' נד: ושם): "ואימא: 'בהמתך' דדברות ראשונות — כלל, 'שור וחמור' — פרט, 'בהמתך' דדברות האחרונות — חזר וכלל!", אע"ג דמרוחקין טובא — היינו משום דעשרת הדברות חשיבי כחד עניינא, דבדיבור אחד נאמרו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 6b:11:1.english: "However, in two matters, one cannot derive" - And that which [the Gemara] asks at the end of [the chapter entitled] HaParah (Bava Kamma 54b and there): "And say: 'Your animal' of the first [set of the Ten] Commandments is a generalization, 'ox and donkey' is a detail, [and] 'your animal' of the latter [set of the Ten] Commandments is a subsequent generalization?" — even though they are very far apart, that is because the Ten Commandments are considered like one matter, as they were spoken in a single utterance.

Tosafot on Pesachim 6b:15:1.hebrew: ודעתיה עילויה - פירוש: ולא בטל מאיליו כמו פירורין. ועל פ"ה קשה: מאי פריך "כי משכחת ליה ניבטלה"? הא פי' "ודעתיה עילויה" שחס עליה לבטלה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 6b:15:1.english: "And his thoughts are upon it" - Explanation: And [therefore] it is not nullified on its own like crumbs. And according to the explanation of the Kuntres, it is difficult: Why did [the Gemara] object, "When you find it, let him nullify it"? For behold, he explained "and his thoughts are upon it" [to mean] that he spares it from nullifying it!

Tosafot on Pesachim 6b:1:1.hebrew: שנאמר ויהי אנשים - והא דאמר בהניזקין (גיטין ד' ס. ושם): "שמונה פרשיות נאמרו ביום שהוקם המשכן", והיינו בראש חדש ניסן, "פרשת טמאים" — לא כפ"ה, דפי' פרשת טמאים "ויהי אנשים", דזו הפרשה נאמרה בערב הפסח, כדמשמע הכא; אלא פרשת טמאים — טומאת תרומה וקדשים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 6b:1:1.english: "As it is stated: And there were men" - And as for that which [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] HaNizakin (Gittin 60a and there), [that] "eight sections were stated on the day the Tabernacle was erected" — and that was on Rosh Chodesh Nisan — [one of which is] "the section of the impure," [this is] not according to the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], who explained [that] "the section of the impure" is [the passage beginning] "And there were men," for this section was stated on the eve of Passover, as is implied here. Rather, "the section of the impure" [refers to] the impurity of terumah and consecrated items.

Tosafot on Pesachim 6b:1:2.hebrew: ומזהיר על פסח שני - אע"ג שעל ידי שאילתו הוזקק לומר להן, מ"מ לא היה צריך להאריך, אלא "אל תעשו פסח" ותו לא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 6b:1:2.english: "And warning about the second Pesaḥ" - Even though he was required to tell them on account of his [the inquirer's] inquiry, nevertheless he did not need to elaborate, but rather [could have merely said,] "Do not make the Pesaḥ," and nothing more.

Tosafot on Pesachim 6b:4:1.hebrew: ממאי דבריש ירחא קאי - תימה, דבשבת בפ"ר עקיבא (דף פו: ושם) קאמר (רבה): דכ"ע בר"ח אתו למדבר סיני; כתיב הכא: "ביום הזה באו מדבר סיני", וכתיב התם: "החדש הזה" וגו' — מה להלן ר"ח, אף כאן ראש חדש. אלמא פשיטא דהחדש הזה נאמר לו בר"ח! והיינו משום דאמר בהקומץ רבה (מנחות כט.): שנתקשה משה רבינו בראיית הלבנה, עד שאמר לו הקב"ה: "כזה ראה וקדש". ותי' ר"ת: אע"ג שאמר הקב"ה למשה בריש ירחא, דילמא משה לא אמר להם לישראל אלא בג' או בד' בירחא. ומסיק דיליף מדבר ממדבר — דבההיא דבאחד לחדש השני, אמירת הקב"ה ואמירת משה הוי בריש ירחא, דכתיב: "באחד לחדש השני", "ויתילדו" וגו'. ור"י מפרש: אע"ג דהחדש הזה הוה בריש ירחא, מיהו דילמא הא דקאמר: "דברו אל כל עדת ישראל" לא הוה בריש ירחא. ואם תאמר: אמאי לא יליף התם מדבר מבמדבר כי הכא? וי"ל: דמדבר מבמדבר לא ילפינן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 6b:4:1.english: From where is it derived that he was standing on the New Moon - It is astonishing, for in Shabbat, in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Akiva" (86b, and there [at 87b]), [Rabba] says: Everyone agrees that they came to the wilderness of Sinai on the New Moon; it is written here: "On this day they came into the wilderness of Sinai" (Exodus 19:1), and it is written there: "This month [shall be for you...]" (Exodus 12:2) — just as there it was the New Moon, so too here it was the New Moon. Evidently, it is obvious that "This month" was said to him on the New Moon! And that is because [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] "Hakometz Rabbah" (Menachot 29a) that Moses our teacher had difficulty regarding the sighting of the [new] moon until the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: "Look at it like this and sanctify [it]." And Rabbeinu Tam answers: Even though the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses on the New Moon, perhaps Moses did not say [it] to Israel until the third or the fourth of the month. And [the Gemara later] concludes that it derives "wilderness" from "wilderness", because in that [case] of "on the first day of the second month", the speaking of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the speaking of Moses were [both] on the New Moon, as it is written: "On the first day of the second month..." (Numbers 1:1) [and] "and they declared their pedigrees..." (ibid. 1:18). And the Ri explains: Even though "This month" was on the New Moon, nevertheless perhaps that which He said, "Speak to all the congregation of Israel" (Exodus 12:3), was not on the New Moon. And if you should say: Why does it not derive there [in Shabbat] "wilderness" from "in the wilderness", as [it does] here? And one can say: We do not derive "wilderness" [midbar] from "in the wilderness" [bammidbar].

Tosafot on Pesachim 6b:8:1.hebrew: אבל בחד עניינא מאי דמוקדם מוקדם - היינו דוקא היכא דליכא דרשה וטעם, דהא תנן בפ' נגמר הדין (סנהדרין מה. ושם) דדחיית הנסקל קודם לסקילתו, אע"ג דסקילה כתיב ברישא, דכתיב: "כי סקל יסקל או ירה יירה" — היינו משום דכתיב במקום אחר סקילה בגמר מיתה, דכתיב: "וסקלתם באבנים ומתו":
Tosafot on Pesachim 6b:8:1.english: "But within one matter, that which is earlier [occurred] earlier" - This is specifically where there is no exposition or reason [to indicate otherwise], for behold, we learned in the Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Nigmar HaDin (Sanhedrin 45a and there) that the pushing down of the one who is stoned precedes his stoning, even though stoning is written first [in the verse], as it is written: "He shall surely be stoned or cast down" (Exodus 19:13) — that is because it is written in another place stoning at the conclusion of death, as it is written: "And you shall stone them with stones that they die" (Deuteronomy 22:24).
